messages:
maria: Quick Q: We're planning to add a \"progress\" (0-100) field to GET /jobs/:id/status. Concern is backward compatibility + cancel semantics. TL;DR: how should servers behave when cancel is called mid-run and when clients poll? Example current status: `{"id":"req-123","state":"running","result":null}`. Proposed: `{"id":"req-123","state":"running","progress":42,"eta_ms":60000}`

alex: short answer: make progress optional and additive. Clients MUST tolerate unknown/extra fields. Servers should keep returning state/result as before. :thumbsup:

priya: agree with alex. Also propose this concrete compatibility guidance for API docs:
```
GET /jobs/:id/status 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "id": "req-123",
  "state": "running",    // enum: queued, running, succeeded, failed, canceled
  "progress": 42,         // optional int 0-100, omit if not applicable
  "eta_ms": 60000,        // optional
  "result": null          // optional, present when succeeded
}
```
Clients should ignore fields they don't understand. Servers must not change enum names or remove result/state semantics without a compat window.

ethan: question on cancel: if client POSTs /jobs/:id/cancel, should we return 200 (canceled), 202 (cancel accepted), or 409 (already finished)? I _prefer_ idempotent cancel that returns 200 with a small body that indicates outcome (e.g., `\{"canceled\":true,\"previous_state\":\"running\"}`) so SDKs don't have to special-case 409s. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

maria: good point. We're seeing different behaviors across services currently. My proposal:
- If job is running and cancel succeeded immediately: 200 + `\{"canceled\":true,\"state\":\"canceled\"}`
- If cancel request accepted but will be processed asynchronously (signals delivered to workers): 202 + `\{"accepted\":true,\"expected_effect\":\"worker will stop soon\"}` + Location header pointing to /jobs/:id/cancel-status (optional)
- If job already terminal (succeeded/failed/canceled): 200 + `\{"canceled\":false,\"state\":\"succeeded\",\"reason\":\"already terminal\"}` (i.e., not an error)
This keeps cancel idempotent and easier for clients.

sam: SDK impact: we need to update the JS/Python SDKs to treat 200 and 202 as non-error for cancel. Also add a small helper `wait_cancel()` that polls status until state==canceled or terminal. Can we standardize the short polling interval and backoff?

priya: propose guidance for polling/backoff: start at 200ms for first 5 polls, then exponential backoff up to 2s, stop after configurable timeout (default 60s). Also recommend clients set a `Client-Request-Id` header for idempotency and tracing.

alex: operational note: on the server side, adding progress means more DB writes/metrics. We should make progress updates batched (workers only update when progress changes by >2% or every 5s) to avoid load. Also ensure we keep the status payload small.

ethan: also consider schema evolution: bump the API minor version? I think not necessary if we follow optional/additive rule. But include a changelog entry and feature flag for telemetry.

maria: ok next: small example of recommended cancel flow for docs (copy-pasteable):
```
# client
POST /jobs/req-123/cancel
-> 202 Accepted
Location: /jobs/req-123/cancel-status
Body: {\"accepted\": true}

# poll
GET /jobs/req-123/status
-> 200
{\"id\":\"req-123\",\"state\":\"canceled\",\"progress\":null}
```
If immediate, return 200 instead of 202.

sam: anything else for SDKs? I'll open a PR to update client behavior and add wait helpers. Ping me for review @maria.

maria: thanks. @ci-bot can you create an API doc issue and link the swagger change?

ci-bot: api-spec: PR opened -> https://git.redwood/api-specs/pull/987 (added progress field, cancel semantics). Auto-generated diff attached.

priya: I'll add a short test matrix for compatibility: old client + new server (should pass), new client + old server (should pass), new client + new server (full feature). Will post tests in the PR.

alex: quick runtime note: when we return progress, ensure we do not leak internal counters or precise timing for security. Keep progress coarse-grained (0-100) and avoid timestamps that reveal internal scheduling.

maria: perfect. Plan: I'll update the API spec per above, Sam will change SDKs, Priya will add tests, Alex/Ethan will add server-side throttling for progress updates. Follow-ups in the PR thread. :thumbsup:
